titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§74–79: Roots and Fish, Begter's Quarrel, the Taichi'ud Return
part: §§74–79 — Roots and Fish, Begter's Quarrel, the Taichi'ud Return
about: Six sections, in three movements. §§74–75 are the widow's years: the Taichi'ud move off and leave Högelün-Üjin with her small sons; she runs up and down the Onan gathering wild fruit and digging roots, and the sons grow up and feed her in turn with fish. §§76–77 are the quarrel over a fish and a little bird, in which Begter and Belgütei snatch the catch from Temüjin and Qasar, the mother's rebuke, and Temüjin and Qasar going out to shoot at Begter. §78 is the mother's tirade (the long run of 'like the beast that ...' similes) and §79 the Taichi'ud's return, the family's stockade in the thick wood, and Temüjin's flight into the forest of Tergüne. The grammar to watch is the converb chain (-žu / -žü / -ču / -ġed, Ming 着, 'having ... -ing'), the possessive -tai / -tei / -tan ('X-having'), the reflexive-possessive (-ban / -jan / -jen / -jüġen / -ġen, 'one's own'), vowel harmony in the case endings, the time-clause in -küi-dür ('while'), and the long metü ('like') similes of §78. The hard places, flagged in their notes, are the two unglossed words of §75 (qaγ̇uluγa, qoġraγ̇ud), the shape of Begter's speech in §77 (the quotation marks do not match), and the kinship wording of Tarqutai's call in §79.

sentences.t: Taičiγ̇ud aqa deġü Höġelün-Üžin-(n)i belbisün-(n)i köġüd üčüged ekes köġüd-i nutuγ-tur gežü negügdežü
sentences.l: Taičiγ̇ud, elder-brothers, younger-brothers, Höġelün-Üžin (acc.), widow (acc.), sons small, mothers, sons (acc.), in-the-camp, casting-aside, being-moved-off,
sentences.i: The Taichi'ud brothers left Högelün-Üjin, the widow, the small sons, the mothers and the sons behind in the camp, and moved away,
sentences.n: Read the §74 opening as one long chain of converbs (-žu / -žü, Ming 着, 'having … -ing') that runs on to the full stop after težiġebe; I cut it into units at the natural joints and each note says where the chain goes. The subject is the Taichi'ud (aqa deġü, 'elder and younger brothers', Ming 兄 弟, here 'the brother-clansmen'); the objects are marked with the accusative -(n)i / -i (Ming 行). köġüd, üčüged, ekes are plurals in -d / -s (Ming 每). gežü is Ming 撇着 'casting aside'; I take it as ge- 'abandon' but it may be the 'say' verb keġe- in an idiom. negügdežü is negü- 'move camp' + the passive -gde-; the Ming 被起着 is 'being made to strike camp'. So the grammar leaves open who moved whom; I read the Taichi'ud as the movers and the widow and children as those left. What ekes köġüd-i means exactly ('the mothers and sons') is my reading of the Ming.

morph.gloss: the Taichi'ud, a people (clan name) [種名]
Högelün-Üjin, a woman's name [婦人名 行]
to cast aside, abandon (or the 'say' verb keġe- in an idiom; uncertain) [撇着]
to move camp, strike camp [被起着]

sentences.t: Höġelün-Üžin eme mergen törežü üčüged köġüd(i)-jen težiġerün ukitala boγtalažu qožitala büseležü
sentences.l: Höġelün-Üžin, woman capable, being-born, her-small-sons while-raising, tight, headdress-putting-on, short-garment, belt-fastening,
sentences.i: Högelün-Üjin, a capable woman by nature, while raising her small sons, put her headdress on tight and belted up her short garment,
sentences.n: A new subject, Högelün-Üžin, and a new chain of converbs. eme mergen törežü is 'woman capable having-been-born' (Ming 婦人 能 生着): 'born a capable woman', that is, capable by nature; törežü is the converb of töre- 'be born'. köġüd(i)-jen is the sons plus the reflexive-possessive -jen ('her own'; Ming 自的行), the first of many: -ban / -ben, -jan / -jen, -ġen, -jüġen all mean 'one's own', and the form follows the stem's vowels and last sound. težiġerün is težiġe- 'rear' + -rün 'while'. ukitala 'tight' (Ming 緊) and qožitala 'short' (衣短) are adverb-like forms in -tala. boγtalažu is boγta, a headdress (Ming 固姑冠), + the verb-maker -la- + -žu: 'putting on the boγta'; büseležü is büse 'belt' + -le- + -žu: 'belting'. The ending of the -tala words is not clear to me; I follow the Ming.

sentences.i: she ran up and down the river Onan,
sentences.n: Onan is the river (Ming 河名); müren is 'river' (河). öġede 'upstream' (逆水, 'against the water') and irada 'downstream' (下水) are a pair of direction words, both ending -de / -da, which read to me as case-like adverb forms; the vowel in the ending changes with the stem (back vowel -da, front vowel -de). güjižü is the converb of güji- 'run' (Ming 走着). The sense, 'ran about along the Onan', is plain from the Ming.

sentences.i: gathering wild pears and moilqo fruit day and night,
sentences.n: olirsun is Ming 杜梨, the 'wild pear'; moilqo is only 果名, 'a fruit name', so I leave it as moilqo. temgüžü is the converb of temgü- 'pick, gather' (拾着). üdür süni, 'day (and) night', has no ending and no 'and': two nouns set side by side, read as 'day and night', as Ming 日 夜 gives them. The chain goes on to the full stop after težiġebe.

sentences.i: and so kept them fed.
sentences.n: qoγ̇olai is Ming 喉嚨 'throat' (also 'gullet'), a bare noun with no accusative ending. 'Reared the throat' is the Ming's literal word for feeding the children, and I read it as 'fed them'; this is my reading of an idiom, since the Ming gives only the two words. težiġebe is težiġe- 'rear' + -be, the plain past (Ming 了); -be / -bi are one past ending, and Shiratori writes both težiġebe and težiġebi (the latter in the next sentence), so the vowel of the ending varies even after the same stem. This is the first full stop of the §.

sentences.t: Sülsütei töregsen Üžin eke sutan köġüd(i)-jen težiġerün
sentences.l: Courage-having, one-who-bore, Üžin mother, fortune-having sons her-own while-raising,
sentences.i: Mother Üjin, who was of stout heart and had borne sons of good fortune, while she reared them,
sentences.n: Sülsütei is sülsü 'gall, courage' (Ming 膽) + -tei, the possessive ending 'having' (Ming 有的): 'courage-having'. This possessive -tei / -tai / -tü / -tu, Ming 有的, is the commonest pattern in this part. sutan is the plural of the same possessive: sutai 'blessed', Ming 福每有的, 'those having fortune'. töregsen is the past participle 'one who has been born / who bore' (生了的); with the Ming alone I cannot tell if it means 'born (with courage)' or 'who bore'; I take 'who bore', since sutan köġüd then follows as the bearing's result. This is a hard reading, so take it as mine. Üžin eke here is the same Högelün-Üjin, now called by Üžin alone, the second part of her full name. The chain then runs through težiġerün into the next unit.

morph.gloss: to be born; to bear [生了的]
past participle: who has … (Ming 了的)
Üjin, a woman's name, the second part of Högelün-Üjin and other women's names [婦人名]
possessive, plural: those having (Ming 有的每)

sentences.t: čigörsün širo barižu sudun, čičigina uqužu težiġebi.
sentences.l: Juniper stake taking, sudun, čičigina digging, she-reared.
sentences.i: taking a juniper digging-stick, dug the roots of sudun and čičigina, and raised them.
sentences.n: čigörsün is Ming 檜木, a conifer (I say 'juniper' as the nearest plain word); širo is 橛子 'peg, stake'. I take them together as a digging tool (the Ming gives only the two materials, 'juniper' and 'peg'; the use is inferred from uqužu 'digging out'); 'digging-stick' in i is that inference. barižu is bari- 'take hold of' + -žu; uqužu is uqu- 'dig out' (剜着) + -žu. sudun and čičigina are only 草根名, 'names of roots', so I leave them as they stand. This is the second converb chain of the §: two converbs, barižu and uqužu, then the final verb težiġebi, 'she reared', ending in the second full stop.

morph.gloss: to dig out, scoop out [剜着]
past: did (the -be form after a front vowel)

sentences.i: Those whom Mother Üjin raised on wild chive and chive —
sentences.n: The next sentence opens with its subject: težiġegsed, 'those who have been reared' (養了的每), the past participle -gsan with the plural -d (Ming 每). Üžin-(n)ü is the genitive -(n)ü, written with Shiratori's (n). qalijarsun is Ming 山薤 'mountain chive'; moṅgirsun(i)-jar is 'chive' (薤) + the instrumental -jar / -γ̇ar, which the Ming glosses 敎 'by means of'. So the line is 'those reared by Mother Üžin on wild chive and chive'. The word that follows, köġüd, is the thing it all hangs on.

morph.gloss: instrumental: with, by means of (Ming 敎)
past participle, plural: those who were … (Ming 養了的每)

sentences.i: the sons came to wish to be sovereigns.
sentences.n: köġüd 'sons' is the head of the phrase begun in the previous unit. qād is the plural of qaγan (Ming 皇帝每, 'emperors'). solura is Ming 願做, 'wish to be' and kürbi 到了, 'arrived': 'they arrived at wishing to be sovereigns'. I cannot parse solura from the Ming alone (it may be a converb of a verb sol-, but I do not know it); i keeps the Ming's wish ('came to wish to be sovereigns'); whether they in fact became sovereigns the words do not say, and I do not claim it. qād is the contracted plural of qaγan, 'sovereigns' as in the published §§7–23.

morph.gloss: sovereign, emperor; qād is the plural, contracted [皇帝每]
to wish to be, to become [願做]

sentences.t: Žarčimtai Üžin eke-jin žaγ̇uγasu-bar težiġegsed köġüd
sentences.l: Orderly-having Üžin mother's lily-root-with those-who-were-reared sons,
sentences.i: The sons whom orderly Mother Üjin raised on lily root
sentences.n: Žarčimtai is Ming 整齊的, 'orderly, well-ordered', with the possessive -tai: 'having order', a name-like epithet. eke-jin is eke + the genitive -jin (after a vowel, as in the earlier parts). žaγ̇uγasu-bar is žaγ̇uγasu (山丹根, the lily root) + the instrumental -bar, back-vowel form of -ber; compare moṅgirsun(i)-jar above, where the -j- shows up: the case endings go -bar, -γar, -jar, -ber, -jer with the stem. težiġegsed köġüd ('those reared, sons') repeats the head of the phrase in §74.

morph.gloss: Üjin, a woman's name, the second part of Högelün-Üjin and other women's names [(母)名]
instrumental: with, by means of (Ming 敎)
past participle, plural: those who were … (Ming 養的每)

sentences.i: became men of law and wisdom.
sentences.n: žasaγtan is žasaγ 'law, ordinance' (Ming 法度) + the possessive plural -tan ('those having'; 有的每): 'men of law'. sečed is Ming 聰明每, 'the wise ones' (a plural in -d). bolba is bol- 'become' + -ba, the past (Ming 做了). The -ba / -be / -bi family is one past ending and its vowel follows the stem; the verb bolba closes the sentence: it is also the last word of §74.

morph.gloss: possessive, plural: those having (Ming 有的每)
wise, clever (as in De-Sečen); sečed is its plural [聰明每]

sentences.t: Γoγ̇a-Üžin-(n)ü γoγosun, moṅgirsu-γ̇ar težiġegsed qaγ̇uluγa köġüd qoġraγ̇ud said bolba.
sentences.l: Γoγ̇a-Üžin's leek, chive-with those-reared, qaγ̇uluγa, sons, qoġraγ̇ud, good-ones they-became.
sentences.i: The sons of Qo'a-Üjin, raised on leek and chive, became good men.
sentences.n: Γoγ̇a-Üžin-(n)ü is the genitive of a woman's name (Ming 婦人名 的); who she is, the Ming does not say and I will not guess; Γoγ̇a is the 'fair' name element of Alan-Γoγ̇a (Qo'a) in the published parts. γoγosun is 韮菜 'leek', and moṅgirsu-γ̇ar is chive with the instrumental -γ̇ar (the vowel and the initial change with the stem). težiġegsed is 'those reared' again. The hard words are qaγ̇uluγa and qoġraγ̇ud: the Ming leaves both unglossed (the Ming has no gloss for them), and I cannot put a meaning to either; qoġraγ̇ud looks like a plural in -d. They stand either side of köġüd 'sons'. In i I leave them out rather than invent; in l I keep them. said is Ming 好的每 'the good ones' (sain, written sayid; the ending -d is uncertain, as in the published parts), and bolba 'became'.

morph.gloss: Qo'a-Üjin, a woman's name [婦人名 的]
instrumental: with, by means of (Ming 敎)
past participle, plural: those who were …
meaning unknown to me (no Ming gloss)
meaning unknown to me (no Ming gloss); perhaps a plural in -d
good, fine (written sayid; ending uncertain) [好的每]

sentences.t: Eres said bolun baražu erekün omoγun ele boldaba.
sentences.l: Men good-ones becoming, finishing, brave, fight-ready, indeed they-became.
sentences.i: They became good men outright, bold and ready to fight.
sentences.n: Eres is 'men' (額舌列思, the plural of er) and said 'the good ones' again. bolun baražu is two converbs: bolun (bol- + -un) 'becoming' and baražu (bara- 'be finished' + -žu) 'having finished'; the Ming 了着 treats baražu as 'completely', so 'fully became'. erekün (敢望, 'daring, bold') and omoγun (與人相鬭, 'fighting with people', so 'ready to fight') are, as I read them, adjectives or nouns of quality; ele 'only, just, indeed' (但) is a particle. boldaba is bol- + -da (a derivation) + the past -ba; the Ming gives 做了 for it as for bolba, and I leave the -da- unexplained. This unit is one of the loosest in the part; the Ming does not give the tie between its words.

morph.gloss: good, fine (written sayid; ending uncertain) [好的每]
to be finished, used up [了着]
ready to fight, 'fighting with others' [與人相鬭]
only, just, indeed (particle; Ming 但) [但]

sentences.i: saying to one another, 'Let us feed our own mother,'
sentences.n: eke-jüġen is eke 'mother' + the reflexive-possessive -jüġen ('their own', Ming 母 自的行). težiġeje is težiġe- + -je, which I take to be 'let us' (the Ming 養咱 is 'rear [we]'). keġeldüžü is keġe- 'say' + -ldu- 'to one another' + -žü (相說着): they spoke to one another. So the sons say to one another, in a converb, 'Let us feed our own mother'. Whether the quotation ends at težiġeje or runs on, the Ming does not show; I close it there.

sentences.i: and they sat down on the bank of the Onan,
sentences.n: eke 'mother' stands here with no ending and no visible role; the Ming adds only (母), in brackets. I cannot place it: it may be a leftover or a repetition from the previous line, and in i I leave it unsaid. Onan-(n)u is the genitive of the river. ergi 'bank' (岸) is followed by deġere 'upon' (上), a postposition. saγ̇užu is saγ̇u- 'sit' + -žu.

sentences.i: readied their rods and hooks,
sentences.n: elgüġür is elgü- 'fish with a hook' (釣) + -ġür, which I take as making the name of the thing used: 'fishing-tackle, rod' (the Ming says only 釣, 'angle'). gügi is 'hook' (鉤). žasaldužu is žasa- 'put right, prepare' + -ldu- (reciprocal / 'together') + -žu; the Ming 相整治着 'preparing each other'. A -ldu- verb occurs again below.

morph.gloss: to fish with hook and line [釣]
noun-maker: the tool for it, rod (Ming 釣)
to arrange, put in order [相整治 着]

sentences.i: and angled and hooked maimed, sickly fish,
sentences.n: eremdeg (殘, 'maimed, damaged') and žemdeg (疾, 'sick') rhyme, as a pair; together, 'maimed and sick', both qualifying žiγasu 'fish': the Ming gives each a single word. žiγasu is 'fish'; elgüžü is elgü- 'angle' + -žü; gügiležü is gügi 'hook' + -le- + -žü, 'hooking' (鉤着). The whole passage in §75 is a list of ways of fishing, each a converb, hanging on the last word of the §.

morph.gloss: to fish with hook and line [釣着]

sentences.i: bent needles into hooks,
sentences.n: žeġü-ber is žeġü 'needle' (針) + the instrumental -ber, 'with a needle', front-vowel form; I take it as 'out of needles', that is, they made their own hooks of needles, since the Ming only has 針 + 鉤 + 曲着. ekeġülžü is Ming 曲着, 'bending'; I take it as ekeġül- (a causative of eke- 'bend') + -žü, but I am not sure of the root. Making hooks out of needles is the sense I give; the Ming does not say 'out of'.

morph.gloss: instrumental: with, by means of (Ming 敎)
to bend, make crooked (root uncertain) [曲着]

sentences.i: and hooked žebüge and qadara fish,
sentences.n: žebüge and qadara are both Ming 魚名, 'fish names'; I keep them as written. gügiležü, 'hooking', as above.

sentences.i: knotted nets and cord,
sentences.n: čilüme is Ming 網, 'net'. kübčileġür is Ming (弦), a supplied 'string'; it ends in -ġür like elgüġür 'rod', so it reads as 'a tool for / made of string', and I take it as a cord or line. hujažu is Ming 結着, 'knotting' (huja- + -žu). I give 'knotting nets, cord'; whether the cord is part of the net or a second thing, the Ming's bracketed (弦) does not say.

sentences.i: and scooped up small fish and fish,
sentences.n: žiramud is Ming 小魚兒, 'little fish' (plural in -d); žiγasu 'fish'. siġüžü is siġü- 'scoop' (撈着) + -žü. The two words for fish stand side by side; the Ming gives each its own gloss, and so do I.

sentences.i: and in return they repaid their own mother by feeding her.
sentences.n: žiči (Ming 郤) is 'but, yet, on the other hand'; i renders it 'in return'. hači is Ming 讎, the same character as for hači 'enmity, vengeance' in the published §§43–63 and in §§77–78 below, where abura- 'repay' (報) goes with it. 'Enmity' cannot be what is reared here, so I read the Ming 讎 in its other sense, 'to requite, repay', and give 'requital': feeding her was how they repaid her. That is a reading of the Ming character, not a settled reading of the Mongol word: hači may be the word of §§77–78 with a sense I cannot see here, or a different word that the Ming glossed alike. eke-jüġen is 'their own mother' (reflexive -jüġen, as above).

morph.gloss: enmity, vengeance (house); here 'requital, repayment' (Ming 讎; uncertain) [讎]

sentences.t: Nigen üdür Temüžin, Qasar, Begter, Belgütei dörben qamtu saγ̇užu
sentences.l: One day Temüžin, Qasar, Begter, Belgütei, four together sitting,
sentences.i: One day Temüjin, Qasar, Begter and Belgütei, the four of them, were sitting together,
sentences.n: nigen üdür is 'one day', the usual opening of an incident. The four names have no ending; dörben (四) is 'four' in apposition and qamtu (一同) 'together'. saγ̇užu is the converb of saγ̇u- 'sit'. The §76 episode is about a fish and a quarrel, and the four sons are the cast. Shiratori marks the names with commas, which I keep.

morph.gloss: Temüjin (a name; the future Chinggis) [(兒)名]

sentences.t: gügi tataqui dotora nigen gegeġen soγosun orožuγ̇ui.
sentences.l: Hook while-pulling, among, one bright soγosun it-entered.
sentences.i: and as they pulled in a hook, a single bright soγosun was caught.
sentences.n: tataqui is tata- 'pull' + -qui, the participle of present time (Ming 扯時 'at the time of pulling'); with dotora 'inside, among' (內) it is 'in the course of pulling'. nigen gegeġen soγosun is 'one bright soγosun': gegeġen (明) 'bright, clear'; soγosun is only 魚名 'a fish name', which I leave. orožuγ̇ui is oro- 'enter' + -žuγ̇ui, the narrative past (Ming 入了); -žuγ̇ui and -žüġüi are one ending (back and front vowel). The Ming says only 入了 'entered'; I say 'was caught' because the hook is in the same clause.

morph.gloss: participle of present time: when … (Ming 時)
inside, within, in the course of [內]
narrative past: did (Ming 了; back-vowel form of -žüġüi)

sentences.t: Temüžin, Qasar qojar-ača Begter, Belgütei qojar buližu abuba.
sentences.l: Temüžin, Qasar the-two-from, Begter, Belgütei the-two, snatching, they-took.
sentences.i: Begter and Belgütei, the two of them, snatched it from Temüjin and Qasar and took it.
sentences.n: qojar-ača is qojar 'two, the pair' + the ablative -ača (Ming 自), so 'from the two, Temüjin and Qasar'; this -ača / -eče is 'from' and its vowel is harmony's. Then Begter, Belgütei qojar is the pair that takes, with buližu abuba: buli- 'snatch, seize' (奪着) + -žu, and ab- 'take' + -ba, the past (要了). buližu abuba is 'snatching, took'; I do not know whether the two verbs are a set phrase.

morph.gloss: Temüjin (a name; the future Chinggis) [(兒)名]

sentences.t: Temüžin, Qasar qojar ger-tür irežü Üžin eke-de ügülerün:
sentences.l: Temüžin, Qasar the-two, home-to having-come, Üžin to-mother, saying:
sentences.i: Temüjin and Qasar came home and said to their mother, Üjin:
sentences.n: ger-tür is ger 'home, tent' + the dative-locative -tür (Ming 裏). irežü is ire- 'come' + -žü. eke-de is eke 'mother' + the dative -de (Ming 行): the Ming's 行 marks 'to a person' (the same case appears as -a in qojar-a and -e in ken-e below), while the dative-locative for places is -tur / -dur after a back vowel and -tür / -dür after a front vowel. ügülerün is ügüle- 'speak' + -rün 'while …-ing', the usual way of introducing a quotation: 'speaking:'. The colon in Shiratori's print marks the opening of the speech.

morph.gloss: Temüjin (a name; the future Chinggis) [(兒)名]
dative-locative: at, to (front-vowel form; Ming 裏)
Üjin, a woman's name, the second part of Högelün-Üjin and other women's names [(母)名]

sentences.t: "nigen gegeġen soγosun gügi žaγ̇γsan-i Begter, Belgütei aqa deġü qojar-a buližu abdaba ba"
sentences.l: One bright soγosun, hook the-one-that-held-in-mouth, Begter, Belgütei, elder-and-younger-brother, the-two-by, snatching it-was-taken. We
sentences.i: 'The one bright soγosun that had taken the hook in its mouth was snatched from us and taken by the two brothers, Begter and Belgütei,'
sentences.n: The speech opens here. žaγ̇γsan-i is žaγ̇- (Ming 啣, 'hold in the mouth, take hold') + the participle -γsan + the accusative -i: 'the one that had taken the hook'. qojar-a is 'by the two' (Ming 兩箇 行): the dative -a marks the agent after a passive, and abdaba is ab- 'take' + -da- (the passive, Ming 被) + -ba: 'was taken from us'. The speaker is the pair, Temüjin and Qasar, so ba (俺) is 'we'; i carries it in 'from us' rather than adding words; the print closes the quotation after ba. The next unit is kēġesü 'when (we) said'.

morph.gloss: to hold in the mouth, take hold [啣了的(行)]
dative: by (the agent after a passive; Ming 行)

sentences.i: When we had said so, Mother Üjin said:
sentences.n: kēġesü is keġe- 'say' + -sü, the conditional / temporal 'when, if' (Ming 說呵; Shiratori writes the long vowel kē- for keġe-). So: 'when (we) said this'. Üžin eke ügülerün: introduces her speech. This conditional ending, -sü / -su (呵), also appears in kündeġesü and orobasu below.

morph.gloss: Üjin, a woman's name, the second part of Högelün-Üjin and other women's names [(母)名]

sentences.t: "Jegügužeġeli aqa-nar deġü-ner jakin tein kildümüi ta.
sentences.l: Don't! Elder-brothers, younger-brothers, why thus do-against-one-another, you.
sentences.i: 'Stop this! You elder and younger brothers, why do you treat one another so?
sentences.n: Jegügužeġeli is a prohibitive: the Ming gives only 休, 'don't!' and I read it as 'stop!'. The form ends in -ġeli, which I cannot identify, and I leave it as one word. aqa-nar deġü-ner are plurals in -nar / -ner (Ming 每), the plural for people and kin, a back-vowel and a front-vowel form, harmony again. jakin tein is 'why, thus'. kildümüi is ki- 'do' + -ldu- 'to one another' + -mui, the present (Ming 相做有): 'do against each other'. ta (您) is 'you' (plural, polite).

morph.gloss: don't!, stop! (prohibitive; Ming 休; form not parsed) [休]

sentences.i: We have no companion but a shadow,
sentences.n: seġüder 'shadow' (影) with the ablative -eče (Ming 外 'except, besides'): -eče here is 'than / except', not 'from'. busu (別) 'other' and nökör (伴當) 'companion, follower'. ügei is the negative 'there is not' (無): the standard way of saying 'none'. No verb is supplied: the line is nouns and ügei. The 'we' of i comes from bi bida in the next unit.

sentences.t: seġül-eče busu čičuγ̇a ügei bi bida.
sentences.i: and no whip but a tail: so it is with us.
sentences.n: seġül is 'tail' (尾), with the same ablative -eče: 'except the tail'. čičuγ̇a (鞭子) is 'whip', and the proverb is: no companion but a shadow, no whip but a tail, the speaker's picture of the poorest state. bi bida is bi (有) 'is, exists' and bida (咱) 'we (inclusive)': 'we are'. Note bida 'we' is a different word from ba 'we' above (俺, exclusive: we without you); bida 'we-all, you and I' includes the listener, so here the mother counts herself in.

sentences.t: Taičiγ̇ud aqa deġü-jeġen γašiγ̇u ker aburaqun bida;
sentences.l: Taičiγ̇ud, elder-and-younger-brothers-own, hardship how repay we;
sentences.i: The Taichi'ud have brought hardship on their own brothers, and how are we to repay it?
sentences.n: This I read as the mother's complaint: aqa deġü-jeġen is 'elder and younger brother' with the reflexive -jeġen 'own' (Ming 弟 自的行), and a reflexive points back to the subject, Taičiγ̇ud: 'the Taichi'ud's own brothers', the family they left, so the speaker is among the injured; γašiγ̇u (苦) is 'bitterness, hardship'. ker aburaqun bida is ker 'how' (怎生), abura- 'repay' (報得) in -qun, which I label future / question only from the sense of 'how shall we …?' (the Ming marks no tense), and bida 'we': 'how shall we repay?'. The verb behind the Ming's 報得 is not clear to me, but it is the same abura- as in §§77–78. The sentence has no verb for 'gave', and the Ming gives none: I supply 'have brought' from the sense, so this is one place where i adds a word.

morph.gloss: the Taichi'ud, a people (clan name) [種名]
ending read as future / question from the sense (uncertain)

sentences.i: and while we speak so,
sentences.n: keġežü büküi-dür is 'having said, in the time of being': keġe- + -žü, then bü- 'be' + -küi, the participle (有的), + -dür 'in the time of' (時). The Ming 有的 時 is the usual shape of the time-clause: 'while (they) are …-ing'. Here, 'while we say "how shall we requite them?"'.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at the time of (Ming 時)

sentences.t: erte Alan eke-jin tabun köġüd metü jakin eje ügeġün bi.
sentences.l: Formerly Alan mother's five sons like, why counsel without is.
sentences.i: Why are you without counsel, like the five sons of Mother Alan of old?
sentences.n: erte (在前) 'formerly'; Alan eke-jin tabun köġüd, 'Mother Alan's five sons' (Ming 婦人名 母 的 五箇 子每), and metü (般) 'like'. Who the five sons were, and why they are named, the Ming does not say, and I do not fill it in. jakin 'why'; eje (商量) is 'counsel, deliberation' (with the Ming's 商量 'consult'), and ügeġün (無每) 'without', a plural of ügei; bi 'are'. I keep the Ming's 般 'like': 'why are you without counsel, like the five sons of Alan?'. Whether the likeness is meant as rebuke or as model I cannot tell from the Ming, so i does not decide it.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (after a vowel; Ming 的)
plural: those (uncertain; no other -ġün in the glossary)

sentences.i: Do not go on like this.' So she spoke.
sentences.n: Ta 'you' and bütügei (Ming 休, 'cease, don't'): I take it as bü- 'be' + -tügei, the wish / command ending of the third person (compare odtuγai in §69). No negative shows in the form, so the sense 'do not' comes from the Ming 休 alone; read strictly it might be 'let it be'. Here 'do not (go on so)'. The print closes the quotation after bütügei. keġebi is keġe- 'say' + -bi (the past, with the front-vowel form -bi, as in težiġebi): 'she said', which closes the mother's speech and §76.

morph.gloss: do not, cease (wish / command form, perhaps of bü- 'be'; the 'not' comes from the Ming 休) [休]

sentences.t: Tendēče Temüžin, Qasar, qojar ülü taγ̇alan ügülerün:
sentences.l: Thence Temüžin, Qasar the-two, not-liking, saying:
sentences.i: Thereupon Temüjin and Qasar, displeased, said:
sentences.n: Tendēče is Ming 自那裏, 'from there' (tende 'there' + the ablative; the long vowel is Shiratori's). It is a narrative joint: 'thereupon'. ülü taγ̇alan is ülü 'not' (不) and taγ̇alan (愛), a converb 'liking, being pleased'; ülü is the negative with converbs and participles, its mate ese is the negative of the finite past. The speech they make opens at Öčigen.

morph.gloss: Temüjin (a name; the future Chinggis) [(兒)名]
not (before converbs, participles; Ming 不) [不]

sentences.t: "Öčigen nigente bižiγ̇ur γodoliduγsan-i tein-kü buližu abulaγ̇a.
sentences.l: Day-before once, little-bird bare-head-shot, thus-too snatching he-took.
sentences.i: 'The day before yesterday, too, when we shot a little bird with a bare-headed arrow, he snatched it and took it.
sentences.n: Öčigen (昨前) is 'the day before, lately'; nigente (一遍) 'once, on one occasion'. bižiγ̇ur (the Ming's (雀兒)) is 'a little bird'. γodoliduγsan-i is Ming 𩪛頭射了的 行: γodoli 'bald, bare' (Ming 禿 in §§24–42) + the Ming's 頭 'head', so I take 'bare-headed', + a verb 'shoot' (射) and the participle -γsan + the accusative -i: 'what was shot with a bare-headed (arrow)'. I cannot read the rare character 𩪛, 'arrow' is my supply, and I do not claim the kind of arrow or that it was for birds. tein-kü is 'thus' + -kü, the Ming's 也, 'also'. buližu abulaγ̇a is 'snatching he took' as in §76, with the past -laγ̇a (了來, 'has come to take'): the Ming marks it as a past with a perfect colour (來), and I say no more. The 'he' is Begter, who is named below. The front of the speech is a reminder of an earlier wrong.

morph.gloss: bald, bare (as in §§24–42; with 頭, 'bare-headed'; the kind of arrow is not stated) [𩪛頭射了的 行]
past with the sense 'has come to': did (Ming 了來)

sentences.i: And now again he has done the same and snatched it away.
sentences.n: edöġe (今) 'now', basa (再) 'again', tein-kü 'likewise', then bulba (奪了) 'snatched', the past of buli-, the same verb as buližu above; bulba lacks the -ži- of buližu; I take it as the same verb in a short form, which is an inference. This is the second wrong: the one with the fish.

sentences.i: How are we to get on together?' they said,
sentences.n: qamtu 'together' (一同), ker 'how' (怎生), alduqun (相過) 'pass (time) with one another', a form in -qun (the same as in aburaqun, future / question), and bida 'we'. I take aldu- as 'to pass, get by' on the Ming's 相過; but the root is not certain from the Ming alone. keġed is keġe- + -d, the converb ending the Ming writes 說了 for. The print closes the speech after bida.

morph.gloss: ending read as future / question from the sense (uncertain)

sentences.i: and, flinging the door aside, went out and set off.
sentences.n: eġüden (門) is 'door'. oγ̇orču is Ming 丟著, 'throwing off, flinging down', with the converb -ču (after -r); γarču is γar- 'go out' (出着) + -ču; jorčiba is jorči- 'set out' (去了) + the past -ba. -ču and -žu are one converb ending; the sound after -r- is -č-.

morph.gloss: to set out, go toward [去了]

sentences.t: Begter hulγun deġere širγa aγta-tan jesün mori qaražu saγ̇u büküi-dür
sentences.l: Begter, little-hill above, pale geldings nine horses, looking, sitting while-being,
sentences.i: Begter was sitting on a little hill, looking at nine pale geldings,
sentences.n: Begter is the subject, with no ending. hulγun is Ming 小獨山, 'a small isolated hill'; deġere 'above'. širγa (慘白色) is 'pale, wan white', the same Ming gloss as γoγ̇ai. aγta is 'gelding' (騸馬); the Ming adds 等 to aγta-tan, which I take as a plural-collective ending -tan (the same as the plural of the possessive -tai). jesün mori is 'nine horses', which I read as 'nine geldings', not 'the nine of them'. qaražu is qara- 'look' (望着) + -žu; saγ̇u büküi-dür is 'while he was sitting', the time-clause as before. The speaker here is the narrator, not the brothers.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at the time of (Ming 時)

sentences.t: Temüžin ümer-eče daldadču Qasar emünēče daldadču
sentences.l: Temüžin from-behind hiding, Qasar from-in-front hiding,
sentences.i: Temüjin hid and came up behind him, Qasar hid and came up in front,
sentences.n: ümer-eče 'from behind' (自後) and emünēče 'from in front' (自前) are the ablative: -eče 'from'; ümer / emün are the 'back' and the 'front' stems. daldadču is Ming 隱着 'hiding' (dalda- 'hide' + -d-, a derivation with the converb -ču). They close on him from both sides. The verb of approach is not in the words: 'came up' in i is supplied from the ablatives and from kürküi-dür in the next unit.

morph.gloss: Temüjin (a name; the future Chinggis) [(兒)名]

sentences.i: drawing their arrows; and when they reached him,
sentences.n: sumu-ban is sumu 'arrow' (箭) + the reflexive-possessive -ban 'their own' (自的行). sambažu is Ming 抽着, 'drawing out'. kürküi-dür is kür- 'arrive' + -küi + -dür, 'when (they) arrived' (到時): the same time-clause as büküi-dür.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at the time of (Ming 到時)

sentences.i: Begter, seeing them, said:
sentences.n: üžeġed is üže- 'see' + -ġed (看著); the converb -ġed (Ming 著) is a second ending beside -žu; the same stem takes -žü in üžežü later, so I cannot say what chooses between them. The speech that follows is Begter's.

sentences.i: '"The hardship of the Taichi'ud brothers we cannot bear;
sentences.n: A speech within a speech. Shiratori's marks do not match: one opens at Taičiγ̇ud, one closes at čidaqun-u, and a second close stands at tebčidkün with no opening. I read one speech of Begter (from ügülerün to tebčidkün) with an inner quotation, Taičiγ̇ud … čidaqun-u, which I take as the others' words that he cites (they are not found in what Temüjin and Qasar said three units before; they are rather the family's refrain, as in the mother's words). i shows the inner quotation in double marks. Taičiγ̇ud aqa deġü-jin is 'the Taichi'ud's elder-and-younger-brothers', with the genitive -jin (Ming 的), and γašiγ̇un (苦) 'hardship'. daγ̇usun (受) is 'enduring' (daγu- with a participle -sun) and jadan (不得) is 'unable', the converb of jada-. So the first half of Begter's quotation is: 'enduring the hardship … unable'. The beginning quotation mark is on Taičiγ̇ud.

morph.gloss: the Taichi'ud, a people (clan name) [種名]
genitive: of (after a vowel; Ming 的)

sentences.i: on whom can we repay our enmity?"
sentences.n: hači 'enmity' (讐, as in the published §§43–63), ken-e (誰行) 'to whom' (ken 'who' + the dative -e), aburan, the converb of abura- 'repay' (報), and čidaqun-u (能麽) 'can (we)?': čida- 'be able' + -qun + -u, the question. The print closes a quotation on čidaqun-u (the inner one; see the first unit of this speech and the note on the unit that follows).

morph.gloss: enmity, vengeance, a feud (Ming 讎, as in 043-054) [讐]
ending read as future / question from the sense (uncertain)

sentences.i: As you say that,
sentences.n: keġežü büküi-dür again, 'while saying' (說着 有的 時). The one who is speaking now is Begter, answering what Temüjin and Qasar have said (the words just quoted); the quotation marks of the print do not match here (there is a closing mark on tebčidkün with no matching opening), and I read from nama-ji on as Begter's own words.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at the time of (Ming 時)

sentences.t: nama-ji jakin nidün-ü surimusun aman-u qaγasun bolγamui ta.
sentences.l: Me why eye's hair, mouth's stalk you-make?
sentences.i: why do you make me a hair in your eye and a splinter in your mouth?
sentences.n: nama-ji is the accusative of bi 'I': nama- (the stem of the oblique forms) + -ji (Ming 將我: the accusative after a vowel). nidün-ü surimusun and aman-u qaγasun are 'eye's hair' (眼的毛) and 'mouth's stalk / thorn' (口約 梗): genitive + noun, twice; this is a way of saying that someone is a nuisance. The Ming 梗 is 'stalk, stiff thing', 'a fishbone in the throat' in Chinese; I give 'splinter'. bolγamui is bol- 'become' + -γa- (the causative) + -mui (the present): 'you make (me) become' (做有).

morph.gloss: I, me (the oblique stem is nama-) [將我]
accusative: marks the object (Ming 將我)

sentences.i: When we have no companion but a shadow,
sentences.n: The same proverb as in §76, now in Begter's mouth: seġüder-eče busu nökör ügei, 'no companion but our shadows'. For the forms see the note at the same words in §76.

sentences.i: and no whip but a tail,
sentences.n: seġül-eče busu čičuγ̇a ügei-dür: the second half of the proverb, with -dür on ügei, 'when there is none' (無 時): the time-clause hangs on a negative, so that the line reads 'when we have no whip but a tail'.

morph.gloss: there is not, none [無 時]
dative-locative: at the time of (Ming 時)

sentences.i: why did you think so?
sentences.n: jakin tein sedkibe ta: 'why thus did you think, you'. sedkibe is sedki- 'think, think of' (想) + -be (了), the past. So the three units read 'when we have no companion but a shadow and no whip but a tail, why did you think so?'

sentences.i: Do not wreck my hearth.
sentences.n: Γolomta is Ming 火盤, 'fire-bowl', which I take as the hearth, the family fire, and so the household. min-u 'my' is the genitive of bi, 'I'. bu is the prohibitive 'don't' (Ming 休) and bürelgetükün is a prohibitive form in -tükün (毀了您) with the 2nd-plural sense 'you (all)': 'do not destroy'. The same bu … -tükün pairs with tebčidkün in the next line. The root is not clear to me; the Ming 毀 'destroy'.

morph.gloss: I (its genitive stem is min-) [我的]
prohibitive, to you (plural): do not (Ming 您)

sentences.i: Do not abandon Belgütei.'
sentences.n: Belgütei-ji is Belgütei with the accusative -ji (Ming 行). bu tebčidkün is 'do not abandon (棄了您)', tebči- 'cast off, abandon' + -dkün, the prohibitive with 'you'. The plea is for Belgütei, who stands with Begter. The closing quotation mark is on tebčidkün.

morph.gloss: prohibitive, to you (plural): do not (Ming 您)

sentences.i: With that he sat down cross-legged and waited for them.
sentences.n: keġeġed is keġe- 'say' + -ġed (說了); žabilan (盤脚) is 'cross-legged', a converb; saγ̇užu 'sitting'; küličēbe is küli- 'wait' + -čē- (unclear; the long vowel is Shiratori's) + -be (the past, 等了). He sits still and lets his brothers come, which is the setting for the next unit.

sentences.t: Temüžin, Qasar qojar emünēče ümerēče ötermeležü odba.
sentences.l: Temüžin, Qasar the-two from-in-front from-behind, as-at-a-butt shooting, they-went.
sentences.i: Temüjin and Qasar went at him, shooting from in front and from behind as at a target.
sentences.n: This time the order is the other way round, emünēče 'from in front' (自前) and ümerēče 'from behind' (自後): they close from both sides. ötermeležü is Ming 近垜子般射着, 'shooting as at a near butt, a target at close range': the verb is ötermele-, whose stem I cannot place (the Ming's 垜子 'target' suggests a noun in it), + -žü. odba is od- 'go' + -ba (去了), so 'went (to him)'. The Ming does not say what the arrows did, and neither does Shiratori's text here.

morph.gloss: Temüjin (a name; the future Chinggis) [(兒)名]
to shoot as at a near butt [近垜子般射着]

sentences.i: They came home, and when they went in,
sentences.n: ger-tür is ger 'home' with the dative-locative -tür; irežü, 'having come'. oroqui-luγ̇a is oro- 'enter' + -qui + -luγ̇a: Ming 入去 呵, 'when (they) went in'; -luγ̇a is a temporal / concessive tail on the participle, 'at the time of'. I take it as a plain time clause.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at, to (front-vowel form; Ming 裏)

sentences.t: Üžin eke qojar köġüked(ü)-ġen čirai uqažu ügülerün:
sentences.l: Üžin mother, the-two her-sons' faces perceiving, saying:
sentences.i: Mother Üjin studied the faces of her two sons and said:
sentences.n: köġüked(ü)-ġen is köġüked 'sons, children' (兒子每) + the reflexive-possessive -ġen 'her own' (自的行); the (ü) is a letter Shiratori marks as supplied. čirai (容顏) is 'face, countenance'; uqažu is uqa- 'understand, perceive' (省着) + -žu. i's 'studied' stands for uqa- 'understand, perceive' (省着, 'examine'). Then ügülerün: opens the speech, and with it the great tirade of the part.

morph.gloss: Üjin, a woman's name, the second part of Högelün-Üjin and other women's names [(母)名]

sentences.i: 'You ruined ones! From my heat, as you came suddenly out,
sentences.n: baraγsad is Ming 廢盡了的每, 'those who are done for, ruined' — the participle of bara- 'be finished' with the plural -d, here used as an insult. qalaγ̇un-ača is qalaγun 'hot, heat' + the ablative -ača (自熱處, 'from the hot place'): 'from my heat' (the Ming says only 'the hot place'; I do not say 'womb'). min-u 'my'; qalad (猛然) 'suddenly'; γarurun is γar- 'go out' + -ur- (a derivation I cannot name; the Ming 出時 gives only 'emerging') + -rün 'while'. The simile that follows (metü, 般 'like') is long; I cut it into short units.

morph.gloss: to be finished, ruined [廢盡了的(每)]
past participle, plural: those who have … (Ming 了的每)
I (its genitive stem is min-) [我的]

sentences.i: you came into the world clutching a black clot of blood in your hands!
sentences.n: γar-tur(i)-jan is γar 'hand' (手) + the dative-locative -tur + the reflexive-possessive -jan 'in your own hands'; the Ming 自的裏. qara (黑) 'black', nodun (血塊) 'clot of blood'. hadqun is Ming 握著 'clutching': hadqu- + the converb -n, as in the published §§55–63. töreligi is Ming 生了來, 'came to be born': töre- 'be born' + a past ending in -ligi that I cannot parse, with the sense 'came to be' from the 來; take my gloss as the Ming's, not as grammar.

morph.gloss: past: came to be (ending not parsed; Ming 了來)

sentences.t: ene qarbisu-ban qužaqu Qasar noγai metü
sentences.i: like this Qasar dog that bites its own afterbirth,
sentences.n: The tirade is a run of similes, each of the shape '[verb] X metü' (metü 般, 'like'); the mother compares her sons to savage creatures that destroy their own. ene is 'this' (這); qarbisu-ban is 'afterbirth' (胞衣) + -ban 'its own'; qužaqu is quža- 'bite' (咬) + the participle -qu 'who bites'. Qasar noγai is Ming 狗名 + 狗, 'a dog called Qasar', that is, a kind of dog: it is the same word as the brother's name Qasar, which may be why the mother picks it, but the Ming does not say so. I translate it 'the Qasar dog'.

morph.gloss: Qasar, a kind of dog [狗名]

sentences.i: like the qablan that charges the cliff,
sentences.n: qada-dur is qada 'cliff' (崖子) + -dur, dative-locative: 'at the cliff'. dobtulqu (衝的) is 'charging, hurling oneself' with the participle -qu. qablan is only 獸名, 'a beast's name', and I keep it. The simile: a creature charging at a cliff.

sentences.i: like the lion that cannot hold down its own rage,
sentences.n: aγ̇ur(i)-jan is aγ̇ur (氣) 'breath, rage' + -jan 'its own'; darun (壓) 'pressing, suppressing' is a converb of dara-; jadaqu (不得) 'unable' with the participle -qu. arslan (獅子) is the lion. 'Hold down its own rage' is my reading of the Ming's 氣自的行 壓 不得, 'unable to press down its own breath'.

sentences.i: like the maṅgüs that speaks of swallowing the living,
sentences.n: amitu (活的) is 'living, a living thing'; žalgisu (呑) 'swallow' — a form I leave open (a verb stem, or the imperative); kēkü (說的) is keġe- 'say' + -kü, 'who says'. maṅgüs (蟒古思) is transcribed from the Ming 莽蛇 'python, great snake'; I keep the Mongol word and do not say what kind of creature it is. i's 'speaks of swallowing the living' follows 活的 呑 說的; I do not make it a quotation, since žalgisu may be a verb stem or a form I cannot place.

sentences.i: like the gyrfalcon that strikes at its own shadow,
sentences.n: seġüder-tür(i)-jen is seġüder 'shadow' + -tür 'at' + -jen 'its own' (影 自的行); dobtulqu 'charging, striking'. šinqor is Ming 海靑, 'sea-blue'; 'gyrfalcon' is the rendering of the published §§55–63, not something the Ming says beyond the name. The simile is a bird that strikes at its own shadow.

sentences.i: like the čaruγa fish that swallows without a sound,
sentences.n: sem(i)-jer is Ming 噤聲的, 'silent, with the voice shut' (the Ming glosses the whole word; I take sem as 'sound, voice' and -jer as an ending with the shape of the instrumental, but how the negative sense arises I cannot say; the form is not clear). žalguqu (呑的) 'who swallows'. čaruγa is only 魚名, 'a fish name', which I leave.

morph.gloss: sem (stem uncertain; read as 'sound, voice'; the Ming 噤聲的 glosses the whole word, 'keeping silent') [噤聲的]
ending (uncertain; the shape of the instrumental)

sentences.i: like the bull camel that bites the hind heels of its own calf,
sentences.n: botoγan(i)-jan is botoγan 'young camel, camel-calf' (駝羔兒) + -jan 'its own'; borbi (後踉) 'the hind heel / hock'; qužaqu 'who bites'. buγ̇ura (風雄駝) is the bull camel; the Ming's 風 may mean 'rutting', but I am not sure and leave it out of l and i. The sons bite what they should protect.

morph.gloss: young camel, camel-calf [駝羔兒 自的行]
bull camel (Ming 風雄駝; 風 uncertain) [風雄駝]

sentences.i: like the wolf that leans on the blizzard,
sentences.n: boroγan-dür is boroγan 'storm of wind and snow' (風雪) + -dür, 'in the storm'; šiγaqu is Ming 靠着, 'leaning on, relying on', + the participle -qu; čino (狼) is 'wolf'. The wolf leans on the storm; I leave the likeness unspoken, since the Ming does not say.

morph.gloss: to lean on, brace against [靠着]

sentences.t: köġüd(i)-jen gelin jadažu köġüd(i)-jen idekü aṅgir metü
sentences.l: Sons-its-own driving unable, sons-its-own eating aṅgir duck like,
sentences.i: like the aṅgir duck that, unable to drive off its own young, eats its own young,
sentences.n: köġüd(i)-jen is 'its own young' (子每 自的行). gelin (趕) is 'driving, chasing', jadažu (不得着) 'being unable', then idekü (喫的) 'who eats' and aṅgir (鴛鴦), the Ming's 'mandarin duck'. köġüd(i)-jen stands as object of both gelin jadažu and idekü, so I give 'unable to drive off its own young … eats its own young'. That is odd as sense; the first köġüd(i)-jen might be 'from its own young' with an object left out, and I do not know.

morph.gloss: son, young [兒子每 自的行]

sentences.i: like the jackal-wolf that defends its own lair if it is disturbed,
sentences.n: kebteši-jen is Ming 窩巢 自的行, 'its own nest or lair'; kündeġesü is Ming 動着呵, 'if (it) is moved / stirred', with the conditional -sü (呵); ömerkü (黨護) is 'taking sides, protective'; čüġeböri (豺狼) is 'jackal-wolf'; I do not identify the animal further. The simile: a beast that turns on whoever touches its den.

sentences.i: like the tiger that seizes and does not hesitate,
sentences.n: barižu 'seizing' (拿着); ülü 'not'; saγ̇araqu (不疑貳的) 'doubting, wavering' with the participle -qu; ülü saγ̇araqu is 'who does not hesitate'. bars (虎) is the tiger.

morph.gloss: to seize, take hold of [拿着]

sentences.i: like the barus that charges recklessly — you are ruined.
sentences.n: balamud (妄) is 'rashly, wildly'; dobtulqu 'charging'; barus is again only 獸名, 'a beast', which I keep. baraba (廢盡了) is bara- 'be finished' + -ba: the verb that closes the string of similes (the speech goes on), and I read it as 'you are ruined' (the Ming gives no subject; 'you' is supplied from baraγsad, 'ruined ones', which opened the speech with the same verb bara-).

sentences.t: Seġüder-eče busu nökör ügei -dür seġül-eče busu čičuγ̇a ügei-dür
sentences.l: Shadow-than other companion none when, tail-than other whip when-there-is-none,
sentences.i: When we had no companion but a shadow and no whip but a tail,
sentences.n: The mother returns to the proverb of §76 as a time clause: ügei -dür, 'when there is none' (-dür written as a separate word, 時, by Shiratori), then the second line with ügei-dür joined. The two clauses depend on what follows. nökör 'companion', čičuγ̇a 'whip'.

morph.gloss: there is not, none [無 時]
dative-locative: at the time of (Ming 無 時)

sentences.t: Taičiγ̇ud aqa deġü-jin γašiγ̇un daγ̇usun jadan büküi-dür
sentences.l: Taičiγ̇ud elder-and-younger-brothers' hardship enduring being-unable, while-being,
sentences.i: and could not bear the hardship of the Taichi'ud brothers,
sentences.n: This repeats the words Begter quoted in §77 (the mother's own complaint in §76 is a nearby variant), with the participle: Taičiγ̇ud aqa deġü-jin γašiγ̇un daγ̇usun jadan, then büküi-dür (的 時), 'while (we) are unable to bear the hardship'. The grammar is that of §77; see there.

morph.gloss: the Taichi'ud, a people (clan name) [種名]
genitive: of (after a vowel; Ming 的)
dative-locative: at the time of (Ming 時)

sentences.i: and were asking on whom we could repay our enmity,
sentences.n: hači 'enmity', ken-e 'upon whom', aburaqun-u (報 的) 'of repaying' (abura- + -qun + -u, which the Ming glosses 的 here, not 麽 as at čidaqun-u, so it reads as a nominal / genitive tail rather than the question particle); keġežü büküi-dür 'while saying'. So the mother quotes herself: 'we kept saying "on whom shall we repay it?"'.

morph.gloss: enmity, vengeance, a feud (Ming 讎, as in 043-054) [讐]
ending read as future / question from the sense (uncertain)
dative-locative: at the time of (Ming 時)

sentences.t: ker aja keġen ein kildümüi ta"
sentences.l: How passing saying, thus you-do-against-one-another, you.'
sentences.i: asking how we should live on, you turn on one another like this.'
sentences.n: ker aja keġen: ker 'how' (怎生), aja (過) 'passing, getting by' — the verb is not clear to me, but the same idea as alduqun in §77 (相過) — and keġen (麽道), 'saying' (keġe- + -n), the usual way of closing a quotation. ein kildümüi ta is 'thus you do against each other, you', as in §76 (kildümüi). The quotation mark closes on ta.

sentences.i: So she spoke to her sons, going back over the old sayings,
sentences.n: keġen again closes the quotation: 'saying'. köġüd(i)-jen is 'to her own sons' (子每 自的行). qaγ̇učin (舊) 'old' and üges (言語每) 'words' (üge 'word' + the plural -s); qadalun (根尋着) 'tracing to the root', a converb in -n. The line shows the mother handing down sayings of the old people, as the next unit says.

morph.gloss: to trace to the root, search out [根尋着]

sentences.i: and quoting the words of the elders, was very much vexed.
sentences.n: ötöküs (老的每) is 'the old ones, elders', the plural of ötögü; with üges (言語每) 'words' it reads 'the elders' words' with no genitive. orkidun (引證着) is 'citing, adducing', a converb in -dun (or orkid- + -un; the split is uncertain). maši (好生) 'very'; maγ̇ulabi is Ming 煩老了, 'wearied / vexed' (the Ming's 煩 is 'to trouble, be troubled'): the mother is worn out, or the sons are vexed — the verb's agent is not given. I say 'she was very much vexed' as the likelier. This closes §78.

sentences.t: Tedüi atala Taičiγ̇ud-un Tarγutai-Kiriltuγ turγaγ̇ud(i)-jan uduridču
sentences.i: Meanwhile Tarqutai-Kiriltuq of the Taichi'ud, leading his companions,
sentences.n: Tedüi atala is Ming 那些 住間, 'while that much …', a time phrase: 'meanwhile'. Taičiγ̇ud-un is the genitive (Ming 的). The name Tarγutai-Kiriltuγ is one man (Ming 人名). turγaγ̇ud(i)-jan is Ming 伴當的每, 'his own companions' (turγaγ̇, the Ming's 伴當 'companion, follower', the same gloss as nökör, with the plural -d and the reflexive -jan; how it differs from nökör I cannot say). uduridču (引着) is the converb of uduri- 'lead' (-ču). The main verb, irežüġüi, comes a few units on, after what Tarqutai says.

morph.gloss: the Taichi'ud, a people (clan name) [種名的]
companion, follower (Ming 伴當; the same gloss as nökör) [伴當的每(自的行)]

sentences.i: 'The wicked ones have shed their feathers;
sentences.n: The speech that Tarqutai-Kiriltuq calls out, in two halves (the Ming 退翎 and 長進 are the hinge). qoluγad is Ming 惡的每, 'the evil ones' (plural in -d). quγ̇ožižuγ̇u is Ming 退翎, 'shed the feathers'; I take it as an image of growing up because the second half says 長進 'advanced, grown', but the Ming does not say so. The ending -žuγ̇u, without the final -i of orožuγ̇ui, I read as the same narrative past (the Ming marks no tense): the first half has the back vowels. The Ming gives no more.

morph.gloss: to shed the feathers, moult (stem uncertain) [退翎]

sentences.i: the droolers have grown.'
sentences.n: šilüged is Ming 涎收不的, 'those who cannot keep back their spittle', that is, small children (šilü 'saliva', + -ged, an ending I cannot name, read as a plural). šiberižuġü (長進) is 'have advanced, grown', with the front-vowel form of the narrative past -žüġü: the second half of the pair has front vowels, the first back vowels (quγ̇ožižuγ̇u), and the endings follow. The two clauses seem to say much the same thing; the Ming gives only 'cannot hold back spittle' and 'advanced, grown'.

morph.gloss: ending (uncertain; read as a plural, 'those who cannot hold it', from the Ming 收不的)

sentences.i: so saying, they came.
sentences.n: keġen (麽道) 'saying' closes the quotation, and irežüġüi (來了) is ire- 'come' + -žüġüi, the narrative past; the front-vowel form (compare orožuγ̇ui, the back-vowel form). It is the main verb of the long sentence begun with Tedüi atala.

morph.gloss: narrative past: did (Ming 來了; front-vowel form of -žuγ̇ui)

sentences.t: Ajužu ekes köġüd aqa-nar deġü-ner šiγui-hoi-dur qorγo lažu
sentences.l: Fearing, mothers, sons, elder-brothers, younger-brothers, dense-wood-in, a-stockade making,
sentences.i: The mothers and sons, the elder and younger brothers, took fright and made a stockade in a thick wood.
sentences.n: Ajužu is aju- 'fear' (怕著) + -žu, 'being afraid'. ekes köġüd aqa-nar deġü-ner is the whole family: 'mothers, sons, elder brothers, younger brothers', in plurals (-s, -d, -nar, -ner). šiγui-hoi-dur is šiγui 'dense' + hoi 'wood' + -dur: 'in the thick wood' (密林裏). qorγo is Ming 寨, 'stockade, fort', and lažu is -la- 'make' + -žu, with the Ming 做着, written as a separate word by Shiratori: 'stockading, making a stockade'.

sentences.t: Belgütei modud quγuru tatalažu šibeġe barižu
sentences.l: Belgütei, logs breaking, pulling-together, a-palisade holding,
sentences.i: Belgütei broke off logs, pulled them together, and set up a palisade,
sentences.n: Belgütei is the subject. modud is mod 'wood' (木頭) with the plural -d, 'logs'. quγuru is Ming 折斷, 'breaking off', a converb I cannot parse (it may be quγu- + -ru). tatalažu is tata- 'pull' + -la- + -žu; the Ming 相扯着 has 相 'one another / together', which would suit -ldu- better, so I cannot say what -la- is here: 'pulling together'. šibeġe is 藩, 'a fence / palisade'; barižu (把着) is 'holding / making' — the pair is 'setting up a fence'.

morph.gloss: (unclear; the Ming 相 suggests 'together, one another')

sentences.i: while Qasar exchanged shots,
sentences.n: qarbulaldužu is qarbula- 'shoot' (a word of the Ming 相射着, 'shooting at one another') + -ldu- (reciprocal, 'each other': an exchange of shots) + -žu. Qasar exchanges shots (相射着); with whom is not in the words (the Taichi'ud, from the context).

sentences.t: Qačiγ̇un, Temüge, Temülün γurban-i žaba žaγ̇ura dürüžu bulγaldun büküi-dür
sentences.l: Qačiγ̇un, Temüge, Temülün the-three, rock-crevice in, entering, mixing-in-strife, while-being,
sentences.i: while Qachi'un, Temüge and Temülün, the three, went into a crevice in the cliff and the fighting went on,
sentences.n: Qačiγ̇un, Temüge and Temülün are three of the children (the Ming: 兒名, 兒名, 女子名; Temülün is a girl). γurban-i is 'the three' + -i, the accusative or a topic marker, as with Höġelün-Üžin-(n)i in §74. žaba is Ming 崖縫, 'crevice in the cliff'; žaγ̇ura (間) is 'among, between'. dürüžu is Ming 入着, 'entering'. bulγaldun (相鬭) is 'contending with one another', a converb in -n with -ldu- (reciprocal): I take it as 'fighting', the fighting between the camp and the Taichi'ud, but the Ming's 相鬭 does not say who fights. büküi-dür 'while' ends the unit. The accusative on γurban makes me think someone is putting the three into the crevice, but dürüžu is not a causative; I have followed the Ming.

morph.gloss: Qachi'un (a man's name; Ming 兒名) [兒名]
Temüge (a man's name; Ming 兒名) [(兒)名]
Temülün (a woman's name; Ming 女子名) [女子名]
accusative or topic marker: as for … (Ming 行)
crevice, cleft in a cliff [崖縫]
to be, exist [有的 時分]
dative-locative: at the time of (Ming 有的 時分)

sentences.i: the Taichi'ud called out:
sentences.n: Taičiγ̇ud is the subject; unšižu (叫着) is unši- 'call out' + -žu, Ming 'calling'. ügülerün: opens the speech.

morph.gloss: the Taichi'ud, a people (clan name) [種名]

sentences.i: 'Temüjin, come to your own elder brother.
sentences.n: Aqa-ban is aqa 'elder brother' + -ban 'own' (哥哥 自的行); Temüžin-i is the name with the accusative -i (帖木只泥). ire is the imperative of ire- 'come' (來). The Ming 行 on both words and the odd sentence order make this line hard: I read it as 'Temüjin, come to (your) elder brother(s)', where the Taichi'ud call themselves his elder brothers, but 'bring Temüjin to your elder brother' would also fit, and I cannot rule it out. The reflexive -ban refers back to the subject of the sentence, here the addressee; read strictly it is 'your own elder brother' (Ming 自的), and who that is — the Taichi'ud speaking of themselves, or someone else — I cannot decide. The accusative Temüžin-i beside the imperative ire is also odd.

morph.gloss: Temüjin (a name; the future Chinggis) [(兒)名 行]
come! (imperative of ire-; Ming 來) [來]

sentences.i: You have no need of the others.' So saying,
sentences.n: Busud-i is busu 'other' (別的) with the plural -d and the accusative -i (Ming 每行): 'the others'. tan-u is ta 'you' (plural) + the genitive: 'your' (您的). kereg (用) is 'need, use', so busud-i tan-u kereg ügei is 'the others, your need none': 'you have no use for the others'. The closing quotation mark is on ügei, then keġen (麽道) 'saying'.

morph.gloss: you (plural; its genitive stem is tan-) [您的]

sentences.i: Called to, Temüjin was put on a horse and fled;
sentences.n: unšiγdažu is unši- 'call' + -γda- (passive, 被) + -žu, 'being called'. Temüžin-i with the accusative is the object of morilaγ̇ulžu, mori- 'mount' (馬) + -la- + -γ̇ul- (causative: 'make mount', 敎上馬) + -žu: 'having been made to mount'. The Ming does not say who sets him on the horse; it is a plain passive-causative, and the agent is not stated. Another reading: Temüžin-i, like odqui-ji below, may be the object of the Taichi'ud's seeing and chasing, with the converbs describing him ('seeing Temüjin, who, being called to, was set on a horse, fleeing …'); i follows the sense and leaves the accusative aside. buruγ̇udγan (迯避) is 'fleeing, taking cover' (the form buruγu- 'flee' + a converb ending I cannot parse).

morph.gloss: Temüjin (a name; the future Chinggis) [(兒名)行]

sentences.i: he ran off into the forest;
sentences.n: hoi-dur is hoi 'wood' (林) with the dative-locative: 'into / in the wood'. duta- (走) is 'run, flee' and γ̇ažu (着) a converb ending that Shiratori writes separately; together 'running off'. odqui-ji is od- 'go' + -qui (participle) + the accusative -ji (去的 行): 'him who went / was going'. The accusative marks it as the object of the Taichi'ud's seeing (üžežü) in the next unit.

morph.gloss: participle of present time: who goes

sentences.i: the Taichi'ud saw him go and gave chase,
sentences.n: üžežü is üže- 'see' + -žü (見着), hüldežü is hülde- 'chase' (趕着) + -žü. Two converbs, and the Taichi'ud are their subject; the object is the accusative odqui-ji from before.

morph.gloss: the Taichi'ud, a people (clan name) [種名]

sentences.i: but when he had squeezed into the thick wood on the heights of Tergüne,
sentences.n: Tergüne is Ming 山名 'a mountain'. ündür-ün is ündür 'high' (高的) with the genitive -ün: 'of the high'; siγui-dur is the thick wood, with the dative-locative. širγužu (鑽着) is širγu- 'push through, squeeze' + -žu. orobasu is oro- 'enter' + -basu, the conditional (入呵), a variant of the -sü / -su (呵) of kēġesü: 'if / when he went in'.

sentences.i: the Taichi'ud could not follow him in,
sentences.n: oron is oro- 'enter' + the converb -n (入); jadažu (不能着) 'being unable'. So 'unable to enter'. The Taichi'ud's pursuit stops at the edge of the wood.

morph.gloss: the Taichi'ud, a people (clan name) [種名]

sentences.i: and surrounded the wood and kept watch.
sentences.n: siγui-dur 'at the dense wood'; horčin is Ming 圍, 'surrounding', from a converb horči- 'encircle'; sakižu is saki- 'guard, watch' (守着) + -žu. Shiratori's text ends the part on this converb, with no full stop, so the sentence goes on into §80.
